title: Emulsions
summary: Fat held as droplets in water, or the reverse, kept apart by an emulsifier such as mustard, egg yolk lecithin or the proteins in butter.

misconceptions.text: Once an emulsion holds, it is stable and can be boiled.

explain: names the three parts: dispersed fat, a continuous water phase and an emulsifier
explains why droplet size and steady agitation decide how stable the sauce is
apply: mounts a pan sauce with cold butter off the heat, a cube at a time, and keeps it glossy
builds a vinaigrette at 3 parts oil to 1 part acid with mustard and holds it through service
discriminate: separates a sauce held by emulsion from one thickened by reduction or by starch
separates a broken sauce from a merely thin one and gives the fix for each
separates a temporary emulsion from one stabilised by an emulsifier

title: Reduction
summary: Boiling water out of a liquid to concentrate flavour, gelatin and body, which concentrates salt and acid at the same rate.

explain: explains that a reduction concentrates salt and acid along with the flavour
explains what gelatin from a stock does to body as the liquid falls

title: Heat control
summary: Matching the energy under the pan to what the food needs: a rate of heat transfer you steer by sound, colour and smell, not a number on a dial.

explain: distinguishes conduction, convection and radiation and gives one pan example of each
apply: preheats a heavy pan to roughly 190 to 200 C for a sear and lets it recover between batches

title: Cooking ratios
summary: The fixed proportions by weight underneath a recipe: 1:1 roux, 3:1 vinaigrette, a 5 percent brine, 3:2:1 shortcrust. They scale where a cup measure does not.

explain: states at least three working ratios by weight and what each one produces
explains why a ratio by weight survives scaling where a volume measure drifts

title: Knife skills
summary: Grip, guiding hand and a small set of cuts held to a consistent size, so every piece on the board cooks at the same rate.

apply: cuts a brunoise, a julienne and a batonnet within about a millimetre of the standard size
keeps the tip on the board and cuts with a forward slicing stroke rather than chopping down

title: Seasoning
summary: Salt used in layers through the cooking, judged by weight, around 1 percent of the food for most savoury dishes, and confirmed by tasting at every stage.

explain: explains what salt does to perceived sweetness and bitterness, not only to saltiness
explains why salt added early has time to diffuse into the food
apply: seasons in layers and tastes at each stage instead of once at the pass
discriminate: separates a dish that is under salted from one that is flat and needs acid

title: Mise en place
summary: Everything measured, cut and placed within reach before the first pan goes on, so that cooking is execution rather than searching.

explain: lists what a station holds: prepped components, tools, waste bin, towels and a wiped rail

title: Stocks
summary: Water drawn through bones, mirepoix and aromatics below a simmer, so gelatin and flavour come out without emulsifying the fat into the liquid.

explain: explains why a stock is never boiled: it emulsifies the fat and clouds the pot
gives working times, roughly four hours for veal or beef and forty five minutes for fish

title: Plating
summary: Composing the plate for the guest and for the pass: hot food on hot plates, clean rims, and a layout that survives the walk to the table.

explain: explains why plate temperature matters as much as the arrangement
explains how the placement of the sauce changes the first bite

title: Kitchen communication
summary: The spoken protocol of a working line: calls and callbacks, corners and hot pans, and saying the problem out loud while it is still small.

explain: explains why every call gets a callback

title: Food safety
summary: Keeping food out of the 5 to 63 C danger zone, cooking to a verified core temperature, and keeping raw product away from anything ready to eat.

explain: states the danger zone, 5 to 63 C, and what the time limits inside it are
gives a verified cook temperature such as 75 C for poultry, or 70 C held for two minutes
apply: probes the thickest part of the product and records the reading in the log
cools cooked food from 60 to 21 C within two hours and to 5 C within four more

title: Cold chain
summary: Unbroken refrigeration from the delivery door to the plate, chilled at or below 5 C and frozen at minus 18 C, logged rather than assumed.

explain: gives the working targets: 5 C or below chilled, minus 18 C frozen
explains why a delivery is probed at the door rather than after it is put away

title: Allergen handling
summary: Treating a declared allergen as a separate workflow: a dedicated station, clean tools, a checked ingredient deck and a spoken handover on every ticket.

explain: explains why an allergen is dose sensitive in a way a pathogen count is not
explains why removing the visible allergen does not make the plate safe
apply: plates an allergen ticket at a dedicated station with clean tools and a fresh pan

title: Cross contamination
summary: Pathogens moving from raw product to ready to eat food along hands, boards, cloths, probes and shared utensils.

explain: names the usual routes: hands, boards, cloths, probes and shared utensils
explains why colour coded boards only work if the whole station keeps to them
